query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small amount of boron (<0.5 at%) into a eutectic high-entropy alloy’s lamellar-colony microstructure, followed by a suitable heat treatment, will strengthen the lamellar boundaries, reduce microcrack nucleation, and produce a measurable increase in room-temperature tensile ductility without compromising or even enhancing yield strength, compared to the undoped baseline.
generation.material_initial_state: An as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies that exhibits limited room-temperature ductility due to microcracking at internal lamellar boundaries.
generation.intervention: Add approximately 0.2–0.5 at% boron to the alloy and perform a subsequent solution-annealing heat treatment within the single-phase region (e.g., ~1100 °C) followed by rapid cooling to achieve targeted boundary modification.
generation.conditions: Standard laboratory casting protocols for the eutectic high-entropy alloy, with controlled addition of boron, then solution-annealing and quenching to fix boron segregation at lamellar interfaces.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron segregation at interphase boundaries, modifying chemical bonding at lamella interfaces and promoting boundary cohesion.
generation.mechanism: Enriched boron at the lamellar boundaries increases local bonding strength, decreasing local crack initiation and propagation sites. This promotes stable plastic deformation in the dual-phase structure, improving ductility without sacrificing overall strength.
generation.predicted_outcome: In tension at room temperature, the boron-doped and solution-annealed alloy will exhibit significantly higher tensile elongation relative to the as-cast baseline, while maintaining or modestly increasing yield strength.
generation.baseline: An as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy with dual-phase lamellar colonies that typically exhibits low tensile ductility (on the order of a few percent elongation) due to interlamellar microcracking.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect of boron doping and solution annealing is limited by boron solubility and process parameters. Excess boron or insufficient solution treatment could lead to brittle borides, negating any ductility improvement.
generation.uncertainty: Exact optimal boron content and thermal processing conditions depend on alloy composition; additional testing is required to determine the best parameter window.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sample sets of the alloy: one undoped baseline and one with 0.2–0.5 at% B doping, both solution-annealed using the same thermal profile. Conduct standard room-temperature tensile tests on both sets to measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and elongation to failure.
measurements: Quantify microstructural changes via microscopy (SEM/TEM) and chemical analysis (EDS) to confirm boron presence and distribution.
Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, and ductility (elongation to fracture).
Compare fracture surfaces to assess microcrack initiation and propagation sites.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped samples do not show a measurable increase in ductility or if their strength decreases compared to the undoped baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
